title: v1.8.0
featureLines: Getting media into the player is now a drag away, and it no longer cares what your files are called.
**Drop files or a folder on the window to load them** (#44). Dropping a folder expands it and starts the slideshow from its first asset — no command-line arguments, no file dialog.

**The stereo layout is worked out from the file itself** (#45). The player reads container metadata and, when that is silent, analyses the pixels — so ordinary LIF, MPO, and side-by-side photos load with the correct layout without being …
Load media by dropping files on the window (#44)
Accept a dropped folder — expand it and start the slideshow (#44)
Detect side-by-side layout from container metadata and pixel analysis instead of the filename alone (#45)
Sobel high-pass + mid-frame seam detector, thresholds calibrated on 2380 real photos (#45)
Assume stereo when nothing identifies a file; the pixel detector becomes opt-in (#45)

title: v0.10.0
featureLines: A large iGPU performance pass: the avatar now holds 60 fps on integrated
graphics, up from 41, by caching the static bubble and pipelining the
silhouette readback. The Vulkan session also moves to
`XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2`, picking up the runtime's late-weave pacing.
Migrate the Windows VK OpenXR session to `XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2` (#55)

title: v0.7.0
featureLines: The Windows Vulkan session moves to `XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2`, so EarthView picks
up the runtime's late-weave presentation pacing with no change in use.
Migrate the Windows VK session to `XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2` (#39)

title: v1.19.0
featureLines: Transparent mode gets a real punch-through region — baked and shaped, with the
chrome hidden and right-mouse drag to move — and the HUD moves to the shared
cached-layer uploader for a cheaper compose. The Vulkan session also moves to
`XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2`, picking up the runtime's late-weave pacing.
Transparent-mode punch-through: baked + shaped, chrome hidden, RMB drag (#82)
HUD via `dxr::CachedLayerUploader` (displayxr-common v2.6.0) (#81)
Migrate the Windows VK OpenXR session to `XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2` (#80)

title: v1.6.0
featureLines: The Vulkan session now runs on `XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2`, so the player picks up
the runtime's late-weave presentation pacing — eye-position latency at weave
time drops to roughly one display refresh with no change to how you use it.
Migrate the VK session from `XR_KHR_vulkan_enable` to `vulkan_enable2` (#43)

title: v2.1.0
featureLines: The weaver now adapts its latency per frame instead of guessing. It consumes the
runtime's measured weave-to-scanout feedback and prefers that over the built-in
heuristic, with `LEIA_D3D11_*` knobs to override on both the D3D11 and D3D12
arms. Paired with the runtime's late-weave pacing, eye position is sampled
much closer to scanout.
Adaptive per-frame `setLatency` on the D3D11 arm (`LEIA_D3D11_*` knobs) (#117)
D3D12 adaptive `setLatency`; couple `N_buffered` defaults to the runtime's late-weave gate (#120)
Consume the runtime's frame-timing feedback — measured horizon preferred over the heuristic (#122)

title: DisplayXR Runtime v2.4.0
featureLines: Default-on **late-weave** presentation pacing cuts weave-time eye-position latency to ~1 display refresh on every present path (measured 62→17 ms D3D12, 96→17 ms Vulkan, 29→17 ms workspace), backed by a new closed-loop measured-latency f…
Late-weave presentation pacing on every in-process path, **default-on** (opt out with `DXR_LATE_WEAVE=0`) (#840)
Weave-latency harness + late-weave phase 1 (env-gated groundwork) (#834)
VK native weave-latency harness + late-weave via `present_wait` pacing (#838)
Runtime-side `present_id`/`present_wait` enablement on `XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2` — Vulkan apps get late-weave with zero app-side code; `cube_handle_vk_win` migrated (#841)
DP frame-timing slot: measured weave→scanout latency fed back to the vendor eye predictor (append-only ABI slot) (#843)
Decoupled presentation: `DXR_PRESENT_OPAQUE` opaque flip present, default-off (#833, #836)

face the viewer, plus an A/B probe for comparing tracked vs. static framing. Built on
the plugin's `DisplayXRProvider.TryGetViewerHead` / `TryGetViewerEyes` API
(displayxr-unity#236), which is the supported way to read the tracked viewer position;
the earlier `Camera.GetStereoViewMatrix` approach returned the same mono matrix for
both eyes under the display provider and silently never tracked.

on the avatar's 3D zone via the plugin's new `SetZoneFeather` API

title: v0.5.0
featureLines: **Breaking.** The DisplayXR extensions are renamed `XR_EXT_*` -> `XR_DXR_*`,
matching the runtime's v2.0.0 train. This is a clean break with no aliasing:
components built against the old names and the new ones do not mix. Upgrade the
whole stack together.
Rename DisplayXR extensions `XR_EXT_*` -> `XR_DXR_*` (DisplayXR/displayxr-runtime#734)

installer is now code-signable end to end, including a two-pass signed
uninstaller.
`SIGN_CMD`-gated installer + two-pass signed uninstaller (#666, #14)
Relicense to Apache-2.0; vendor-neutral `NOTICE`

title: v0.5.0 — UE over IPC + first-class shell citizen
featureLines: **Render over IPC (shell / forced-IPC)** via a canonical `arraySize=2` stereo array swapchain (the single-tiled shared texture is non-coherent cross-process from UE's process). Resolves the 0.4.3 "content arrives black at the service com…
**Camera-look under the shell** — driven straight on the local `PlayerController` (`AddYaw/PitchInput`), since UE routes mouse by capture/cursor-position and is never foreground under the shell.
**Keyboard input** relayed to UE's window (WASD/QE); Ctrl is swallowed (reserved for shell chords; UE's default pawn binds it to vertical movement).
